Sample Size Necessary for the Accuracy in Parameter Estimation Approach for an Unstandardized Regression Coefficient of Interest

Source: R/ss_aipe_rc.R
ss_aipe_rc.Rd

A function used to plan sample size from the accuracy in parameter estimation perspective for an unstandardized regression coefficient of interest given the input specification.

Usage

ss_aipe_rc(
  true_R2_Y_X = NULL,
  true_R2_j_X_without_j = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  true_reg_coef_j = NULL,
  width,
  which_width = "Full",
  true_sd_Y = 1,
  true_sd_X = 1,
  true_cor_XX = NULL,
  true_cor_YX = NULL,
  which_predictor = NULL,
  alpha_lower = NULL,
  alpha_upper = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  assurance_method = "analytic"
)

Arguments

true_R2_Y_X

Population value of the squared multiple correlation coefficient

true_R2_j_X_without_j

Population value of the squared multiple correlation coefficient predicting the jth predictor variable from the remaining p-1 predictor variables

p

The number of predictor variables

true_reg_coef_j

The population regression coefficient for the jth predictor variable (i.e., the predictor of interest), in the units true_sd_Y and true_sd_X describe: the standardized coefficient times true_sd_Y / true_sd_X. On the covariance structure path it may be left out; when it is given it must equal that value (see ss_aipe_reg_coef)

width

The desired width of the confidence interval

which_width

Which Width ("Full", "Lower", or "Upper") the width refers to (at present, only "Full" can be specified)

true_sd_Y

The population standard deviation of Y (i.e., the dependent variable)

true_sd_X

The population standard deviation of the jth X variable (i.e., the predictor variable of interest)

true_cor_XX

Population correlation matrix for the p predictor variables

true_cor_YX

Population p length vector of correlation between the dependent variable (Y) and the p independent variables

which_predictor

Identifies which of the p predictors is of interest

alpha_lower

Type I error rate for the lower confidence interval limit, at least 1e-9 and at most .5; a tail area below 1e-9 is refused, as in ss_aipe_reg_coef

alpha_upper

Type I error rate for the upper confidence interval limit, at least 1e-9 and at most .5

conf_level

Desired level of confidence for the computed interval (i.e., 1 - the Type I error rate); a level above .999999998, whose tail areas are below 1e-9, is refused

assurance

Optional probability with which the realized confidence interval is to be no wider than width; when NULL (the default) the plan is for the width of the interval at the expected values of the sample squared multiple correlations (see ss_aipe_reg_coef), not for the mean width over samples

assurance_method

How the probability that the realized interval is no wider than width is found, used only with assurance. Only "analytic" (the default) is offered here: the probability is computed exactly (an F probability) and reported as assurance_attained, and the plan is the smallest sample size, at or above the plan without assurance, at which it is at least assurance. "simulation", which ss_aipe_sc_ancova, ss_aipe_reg_coef with noncentral = TRUE, and ss_aipe_src offer, where the probability has no exact form, is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid. See "The assurance step" in ss_aipe_reg_coef.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value: necessary_N, the necessary total sample size; with assurance, the rows assurance and assurance_attained, the exact probability at necessary_N that the realized interval is no wider than width. With assurance the printed footer names the assurance method, which the attribute assurance_method records, with assurance_probability "exact".

Details

Not all of the arguments need to be specified, only those that provide all of the necessary information so that the sample size can be determined for the conditions specified.

The interval planned for is the central t interval for the coefficient in the units of the data, the interval ci_rc reports, for random predictors from a multivariate normal population, with the t quantiles of its two tails. The plan without assurance is the smallest sample size, of at least \(p + 2\), at which that interval, at the expected squared multiple correlations, is no wider than width; it can be a case or more smaller than that of MBESS (see ss_aipe_reg_coef). With assurance the plan is the smallest sample size at which that interval is no wider than width with at least that probability, computed exactly (assurance_method = "analytic"). The published chi square approximation of Kelley and Maxwell (2003) can give a smaller or a larger sample size than the exact plan.

Note

This function calls upon ss_aipe_reg_coef in DMAR but has a different naming scheme. See ss_aipe_reg_coef for more details.

References

Kelley, K., & Maxwell, S. E. (2003). Sample size for multiple regression: Obtaining regression coefficients that are accurate, not simply significant. Psychological Methods, 8(3), 305–321. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.8.3.305

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapter 4 on individual comparisons of means and Chapter 6 on trend analysis.)

See also

ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity, ci_nc_t, ss_aipe_reg_coef, ss_aipe_src

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Exchangeable correlation structure
true_cor_YX <- c(.3, .3, .3, .3, .3)
true_cor_XX <- rbind(c(1, .5, .5, .5, .5), c(.5, 1, .5, .5, .5), c(.5, .5, 1, .5, .5),
c(.5, .5, .5, 1, .5), c(.5, .5, .5, .5, 1))

ss_aipe_rc(width = .1, which_width = "Full", true_sd_Y = 1, true_sd_X = 1,
           true_cor_XX = true_cor_XX,
           true_cor_YX = true_cor_YX, which_predictor = 1, conf_level = 1 - .05)
#>  term        value
#>  necessary_N 2184 
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# The smallest N at which the interval is no wider than .1 with
# probability at least .85; the last row is that probability.
ss_aipe_rc(width = .1, which_width = "Full", true_sd_Y = 1, true_sd_X = 1,
           true_cor_XX = true_cor_XX,
           true_cor_YX = true_cor_YX, which_predictor = 1, conf_level = 1 - .05, assurance = .85)
#>  term               value
#>  necessary_N        2281 
#>  assurance          0.850
#>  assurance_attained 0.850
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: analytic; assurance_attained is the exact probability that the interval is no wider than the width

# In the units of the data (Y with standard deviation 10, the predictor
# with standard deviation 2), a width of .1 * 10 / 2 gives the same plan.
ss_aipe_rc(width = .5, true_sd_Y = 10, true_sd_X = 2, true_cor_XX = true_cor_XX,
           true_cor_YX = true_cor_YX, which_predictor = 1, assurance = .85)
#>  term               value
#>  necessary_N        2281 
#>  assurance          0.850
#>  assurance_attained 0.850
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: analytic; assurance_attained is the exact probability that the interval is no wider than the width
